transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO - ShadowBay), Markus Chen (Lead ML Eng), Lina Gomez (Platform Eng)
Notes/links referenced: ShadowBay intake deck (link: https://app.shared/decks/shadowbay-intake), Redwood dedicated whitepaper (link), warm-pool benchmark sheet (will be shared)

[00:00] Samira (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda: we want to understand your latency SLOs, burst profile, and constraints so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private. also introduce jordan who will dig into infra details.
[00:18] Priya (CTO): Thanks Samira. quick intro — ShadowBay is building clinical summarization and triage for telehealth, so latency and PII controls matter. we currently run a mix of hosted APIs and some onprem for PHI. exploring Redwood for a dedicated footprint.
[00:32] Jordan (SE): great context. Markus, can you paint the traffic shape? steady vs big spikes?
[00:38] Markus (Lead ML): sure. baseline is ~80 qps during business hours, with 10-15% variability day-to-day. but we see event-driven spikes — typically 5x for 15-30 minutes after promo blasts or morning consult windows. so bursts to 400 qps occasionally. thresholds are fuzzy, that's why we're evaluating reserved capacity + warm pools.
[00:58] Priya: yes, and the risk is those spikes are user-facing — 99th percentile latency must stay under 450ms for short responses, and we need consistent throughput for long summaries (up to 1k tokens). also, cost is a big constraint — can't double spend on cold capacity.
[01:15] Jordan: ok. two levers we usually recommend: reserved GPUs (guaranteed baseline) + warm-pool nodes that prewarm KV caches for fast startup, with controlled burst capacity. for 1k token workloads, batching choices matter. are your prompts typically short or long?
[01:29] Markus: mixture — triage snippets usually ~150 tokens, end-to-end summarization can hit 900-1k. majority are shorter. our current infra uses TensorRT-optimized models on A10s for much of the load.
[01:42] Lina (Platform): infra note: we require VPC peering for any dedicated/private deployment and KMS-managed keys. SOC2 compliance and audit logs are gating for procurement.
[01:55] Samira: understood — Redwood Dedicated supports VPC-hosted private plane, KMS integration and audit logs. we also have SOC2 and ISO docs, i'll share them. quick Q: are you open to a hybrid where critical PHI routes to private nodes and general traffic goes to hosted?
[02:12] Priya: yes, that would be ideal. would we be double-billed? how does routing and failover happen?
[02:20] Jordan: good question. routing is policy-driven — you can pin routes (by tenant, api key, or path) to private or dedicated pools. failover policies can send overflow to a cold fallback (lower-cost variant) or to hosted if you allow it. cost-wise you pay for reserved capacity and only for burst usage when we provision extra burst nodes — there's a delta charge. we can model it in the pricing spreadsheet.
[02:40] Markus: about cold start — how quickly can a warm node accept traffic for a 1k token request? we saw 2-3s cold starts on other providers which is not acceptable.
[02:49] Jordan: warm-pool nodes keep model weights and KV caches resident, so typical warm to accept is 100-200ms for initial token generation. cold start (from scaled-to-zero) can be multiple seconds. that's why for predictable spikes we recommend a small warm pool sized to cover X% of expected burst. note: exact numbers vary by model and quantization.
[03:08] Priya: hmm. Markus, what's acceptable? 200ms would be nice. 450ms 99th overall.
[03:14] Markus: 450ms 99th is our must-have for short ops. for long summaries, 99th within 1.2s might be tolerable.
[03:20] Jordan: good, those are achievable with dedicated pools plus batching controls. tradeoff: batching improves throughput and reduces cost but increases per-request tail latency if you wait to accumulate tokens. we can set dynamic batching thresholds and max batch latency.
[03:35] Samira: can you walk through a sample capacity recommendation? e.g., baseline 80 qps with 5x bursts to 400 qps.
[03:42] Jordan: sure — quick back-of-envelope: assume model throughput per A100-equivalent node is ~100 qps for mixed prompt distribution at single-token latency goals (very approximate). for baseline 80 qps, 1 node might suffice but for headroom and failovers we recommend reserving 2 nodes. for spikes to 400 qps, we'd rely on warm-pool + burst nodes — reserve 4 nodes and allow burst to scale to 6-8 nodes. exact counts depend on model selection, sequence length distribution, and quantization profiles.
[04:08] Markus: does Redwood support mixed instance types? we have some onprem A10s and could want a hybrid.
[04:15] Jordan: yes, dedicated supports heterogenous fleets and can map models to optimum hardware. hybrid private+hosted is common. provisioning onprem requires heavier onboarding.
[04:22] Lina: procurement will ask about eviction/preemption during cloud shortages. what happens to tenant isolation when the provider preempts?
[04:29] Jordan: dedicated reserved capacity is non-preemptible for the reserved pool. burst nodes that come from shared capacity may be preemptible depending on the contract. we provide topologies with tenant fencing to limit blast radius — e.g., strict node reservations and per-tenant quotas.
[04:40] Priya: security question — how do you handle logs and PII? we need audit logs that don't leak prompt content to third parties and need retention controls.
[04:49] Samira: Redwood can store audit logs in your VPC or ship them to your SIEM; we also support redaction rules and allow customers to opt-out of retention. KMS-managed encryption for model keys and payloads is available in Private mode.
[05:02] Markus: what about model fallbacks? If a model variant isn't available during spikes, do we degrade gracefully or fail requests?
[05:10] Jordan: routing policies allow automatic fallback to smaller models (quantized) or to hosted equivalent. there's a configurable policy: fail closed vs fail open with lower-quality model. we can do canary routing too.
[05:20] Priya: procurement will also ask about SLA credits — what uptime and latency SLOs are contractually supported?
[05:26] Samira: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and best-effort latency targets. exact numbers depend on capacity commitment. we'll include typical SLO language in the contract draft. for latency SLOs we'd commit to a percentile on reserved capacity and provide observability for diagnostics.
[05:41] Markus: curious about cost math — do you have a model showing tokens cost vs reserved-node cost? we need to show finance a TCO for 12 months.
[05:50] Samira: yes, we'll produce a TCO modeling sheet: reserved node amortization, burst unit rates, and estimated token costs. we'll need your traffic histogram to make it accurate.
[05:58] Lina: for VPC peering, what's the typical lead time and what do you need from our infra team?
[06:03] Jordan: normally 2-3 weeks for dedicated private with peering and KMS setup. we'll need CIDR ranges, bastion/access plan, and KMS key ARNs. for on-prem it's longer.
[06:12] Priya: timeline-wise, we'd like a pilot in October if possible. procurement window is late Sep.
[06:18] Samira: good. suggested pilot: 3 months, reserved min 4 GPUs with 2 warm pool nodes, run 2-hr PoC with your top traffic slice. dovetail SOC2 docs and pricing.
[06:27] Markus: sounds reasonable. one more technical: KV cache size and eviction — when you prewarm, do you get prefix caching across requests from same user? we rely heavily on KV caching for longer conversations.
[06:37] Jordan: yes, we support prefix/KV caching and sticky routing to warm nodes for cache locality. eviction policies vary by memory constraints — we can show expected cache hit rates for your traffic during the PoC. note: cross-tenant KV caching is disabled for strict isolation.
[06:51] Priya: any gotchas around batch sizing for long summaries? we tried large batches and saw tokenization overhead spike.
[06:58] Jordan: that can happen. for long sequences, we often trade to smaller max batch sizes but allow multiple tokens/per-step throughput. quantization and specific kernel choices matter. we'll run benchmarks with your prompt set.
[07:09] Samira: ok quick recap before Q/A: (1) we propose reserved baseline + warm pool + burst policy (2) hybrid routing so PHI stays private (3) 2-3 week peering lead time and pilot in Oct (4) Jordan will share benchmarks and warm-pool sheet, Samira to send pricing + SOC2 docs.
[07:27] Priya: yep. two final Qs: can we simulate failure scenarios — like region outage — and test failover to hosted in the pilot?
[07:34] Jordan: absolutely — we can run chaos scenarios during the PoC and measure end-to-end behavior. we'll demo canary rollouts and fallback.
[07:41] Markus: and latency monitoring — we need token-level traces and attribution for cost centers.
[07:47] Samira: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. we'll give you access to a demo org.
[07:54] Lina: ok thanks. procurement person will be joining next week, i'll loop them into the slack channel.
[07:59] Samira: perfect — action items and deadlines are in the notes; we'll follow up by Friday. thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present — e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache, "S L A" written as letters. speaker overlaps around 06:30 were brief.

End of transcript.
